trails.name: The Kerry Way
trails.why: The Kerry Way is a long-distance trail in County Kerry, Ireland. It is a 214-kilometre long circular trail that begins and ends in Killarney.

trails.name: Beara Way
trails.why: The Beara Way is a long-distance trail in the southwest of Ireland. It is a 206-kilometre long circular trail around the Beara Peninsula that begins and ends in Glengarriff, County Cork, also passing through parts of County Kerry.

trails.name: East Clare Way
trails.why: The East Clare Way is a long-distance trail in County Clare, Ireland. It is a 180-kilometre long circular route that begins and ends in Killaloe.

trails.name: The Dingle Way
trails.why: The Dingle Way is a long-distance trail around the Dingle Peninsula in County Kerry, Ireland.

trails.name: Mid Clare Way
trails.why: The Mid Clare Way is a long-distance trail in County Clare, Ireland. It is a 148-kilometre long circular route that begins and ends in Newmarket-on-Fergus.

trails.name: Miners Way & Historical Trail
trails.why: The Miners' Way and Historical Trail is a long-distance trail in Ireland. It is a 118-kilometre long circular route that begins and ends in Arigna, County Roscommon.

trails.name: Wicklow Way
trails.why: The Wicklow Way is a long-distance trail that crosses the Wicklow Mountains in Ireland. It runs from Marlay Park in the southern suburbs of Dublin through County Wicklow and ends in the village of Clonegal in County Carlow.

trails.name: Suck Valley Way
trails.why: The Suck Valley Way is a long-distance trail in Ireland. It is a 105-kilometre long circular route that begins and ends in Castlerea, County Roscommon.

trails.name: The Barrow Way
trails.why: The Barrow Way is a long-distance trail in Ireland.

trails.name: South Leinster Way
trails.why: The South Leinster Way is a long-distance trail in Ireland. It is 104 kilometres long and begins in Kildavin, County Carlow and runs through County Kilkenny before ending in Carrick-on-Suir, County Tipperary.

trails.name: Ballyhoura Way
trails.why: The Ballyhoura Way is a long-distance trail in Ireland. It is 89 kilometres long and begins at St John’s Bridge, near Kanturk, County Cork and ends at Limerick Junction, County Tipperary.

trails.name: Sheep's Head Way
trails.why: The Sheep's Head Way is one of Ireland's newest hiking trails.

trails.name: Sligo Way
trails.why: The Sligo Way is a long-distance trail mainly in County Sligo, Ireland. It is 78 kilometres long and begins in Larrigan, near Lough Talt and ends in Dromahair, County Leitrim.

trails.name: Errigal Way - Donegal Way
trails.why: Bealach na Gaeltachta, Dún na nGall comprises four circular long-distance trails in the Gaeltacht areas of County Donegal Republic of Ireland.

trails.name: Slieve Bloom Way

trails.name: East Munster Way
trails.why: The East Munster Way, formerly known as the Munster Way, is a long-distance trail in Ireland.

trails.name: Lough Derg Way
trails.why: The Lough Derg Way is a long-distance trail in Ireland. It is 68 kilometres long and begins in Limerick City and ends in Dromineer, County Tipperary.

trails.name: Monaghan Way
trails.why: The Monaghan Way is a long-distance trail in County Monaghan, Ireland. It is 65-kilometre long and begins in Monaghan Town and ends in Inniskeen.

trails.name: Colmcille's Way - Donegal Way
trails.why: Bealach na Gaeltachta, Dún na nGall comprises four circular long-distance trails in the Gaeltacht areas of County Donegal Republic of Ireland.

trails.name: Bluestack Way
trails.why: The Bluestack Way is a long-distance trail through the Bluestack Mountains in County Donegal, Ireland.

trails.name: Finn's Way - Donegal Way

trails.name: Slieve Felim Way
trails.why: The Slieve Felim way is a long-distance trail through the Slieve Felim Mountains in Ireland.

trails.name: North Kerry Way
trails.why: The North Kerry Way is a long-distance trail in County Kerry, Ireland. It is 45 kilometres long and begins in Tralee and ends in Ballyheigue.

trails.name: Dublin Mountains Way
trails.why: The Dublin Mountains Way is a waymarked long-distance trail in the Dublin Mountains, Counties South Dublin and Dún Laoghaire–Rathdown, Ireland.

trails.name: Táin Way
trails.why: The Táin Way is a long-distance trail around the Cooley Peninsula in County Louth, Ireland.

trails.name: The Offaly Way
trails.why: The Offaly Way is a long-distance trail in County Offaly, Ireland. It is 37 kilometres long and begins in Cadamstown and ends at Lemanaghan, on the R436 road between the towns of Clara and Ferbane.

trails.name: Limerick Greenway
trails.why: A 39km off-road walking and cycling route along a former railway line that connects Rathkeale, Newcastle West and Abbeyfeale

trails.name: Multeen Way
trails.why: The Multeen Way is a long-distance trail in County Tipperary, Ireland. It is 23 kilometres long and begins in Tipperary Town and ends in Upperchurch.

trails.name: Westmeath Way
trails.why: The Westmeath Way is a long-distance trail in County Westmeath, Ireland. It is 100 kilometres long and begins in Kilbeggan and ends in Athlone.

trails.name: Saint Kevin's Way
trails.why: From Hollywood to Glendalough. St Kevin's Way follows in the footsteps of St Kevin through the hills of County Wicklow to the valley of Glendalough where he stayed the rest of his life.

trails.name: Bangor Trail
trails.why: The Bangor Trail is a waymarked walking trail in Erris, North Mayo, Ireland.

trails.name: Cavan Way
trails.why: The Cavan Way is a long-distance trail in County Cavan, Ireland. It is 22 kilometres long and begins in Blacklion and ends in Dowra.

trails.name: Boyne Valley Camino
trails.why: A figure of eight looped walk from Drogheda to Mellifont Abbey and back

trails.name: Nore Valley Way: Thomastown - Inistioge

trails.name: Nore Valley Way: Kilkenny - Bennetsbridge
trails.why: The Nore Valley Way is a long-distance trail under development in County Kilkenny, Ireland.

trails.name: Trawlebane Walk
trails.why: Drimoleague, which was once the busiest railway junction in West Cork with no fewer than three platforms, has now become the hub of walking networks in the area.

trails.name: Valley Loop Walk
trails.why: Slí Tóin a' tSeanbhaile / Valley Loop Walk is an 8.5km looped walk on coastal ground with no hills or climbs.

trails.name: Glanatnaw Walk

trails.name: Castlemorris Pheasant Loop
trails.why: Castlemorris Loops Difficulty Easy | Distance 7km | Ascent 90-160m | Time 2-2.5h | Type Loop A series of 3 woodland loop walks between 3km and 7km.

trails.name: Freshford Loop
trails.why: Freshford Loop Difficulty Moderate | Distance 6km | Ascent 100m | Time 1.5h | Type Loop Starting from the picturesque village green, this 6km loop walk takes you along woodland tracks and open farmland, with the final section following the Nuenna River.

trails.name: Bray Head Loop
trails.why: The Bray Head Loop is a 5.5km route and offers spectacular views of Bray, North East Wicklow, Dublin Bay and the Irish Sea.

trails.name: Glanbannoo Walk
trails.why: Drimoleague, which was once the busiest railway junction in West Cork with no fewer than three platforms, has now become the hub of walking networks in the area.

trails.name: Courtmacsherry Loop
trails.why: Partially wooded walk with sea views and lined with deep purple fuchsia in September

trails.name: Belmont Way
trails.why: The Belmont Way is a 5.5km route that offers a varied, and at times, challenging walk, through some of north Wicklow’s most interesting landscape that includes native woodland, farmland and the shoulder of The Little Sugarloaf and its commanding views.

trails.name: Mullaghmeen Blue Walk
trails.why: A superb recreation site with three trails and a multi access trail in the largest beech forest in Ireland.

trails.name: The Sugar Loaf Way
trails.why: The ambitious vision to develop and map a series of walks on designated trails that will take visitors and locals from Bray DART / Bus Station to Rathdrum train station is a step closer with the recent development of The Sugar Loaf Way.

trails.name: O'Gorman's Lane Loop
trails.why: O’Gorman’s Lane Loop Difficulty Easy | Distance 4km | Ascent 20-60m | Time 1h | Type Loop This is a short loop walk starting and finishing in the village of Bennettsbridge.

trails.name: Knocknapeasta summit
trails.why: Cnoc na Péiste, anglicised Knocknapeasta, at 988 metres, is the fourth-highest peak in Ireland, on the Arderin and Vandeleur-Lynam lists.

trails.name: Cnoc an Chuillinn summit
trails.why: Cnoc an Chuillinn, at 958 metres, is the sixth-highest peak in Ireland on the Arderin list and the seventh-highest peak in Ireland on the Vandeleur-Lynam list.

trails.name: Lugnaquilla summit
trails.why: Lugnaquilla, at 925 metres, is the 11th–highest peak in Ireland on the Arderin list, and 13th–highest on the Vandeleur-Lynam list, and the highest Irish mountain outside of Kerry.

trails.name: Mullaghcleevaun summit
trails.why: Mullaghcleevaun at 849 metres, is the 15th–highest peak in Ireland on the Arderin scale, and the 20th–highest peak on the Vandeleur-Lynam scale.

trails.name: Purple Mountain summit
trails.why: Purple Mountain at 832 metres high, is the 21st–highest peak in Ireland on the Arderin scale, and the 28th–highest according to the Vandeleur-Lynam scale.

trails.name: Mweelrea summit
trails.why: Mweelrea at 814 metres, is the 26th-highest peak in Ireland on the Arderin scale, and the 34th-highest peak on the Vandeleur-Lynam scale.

trails.name: Ben Lugmore summit
trails.why: Ben Lugmore at 803 metres is the 29th-highest peak in Ireland on the Arderin scale, and the 37th-highest peak on the Vandeleur-Lynam scale.

trails.name: Cloghernagh summit
trails.why: Cloghernagh at 800 metres, does not have the prominence to qualify as an Arderin, but does have the prominence to be the 40th–highest peak on the Vandeleur-Lynam scale.

trails.name: Kilclooney Mountain summit
trails.why: Fauscoum, also known as Kilclooney Mountain, is a mountain in County Waterford, Ireland. It is the highest mountain of the Comeragh Mountain Range and the second highest mountain in County Waterford after Knockmealdown.

trails.name: Slievemaan summit
trails.why: Slievemaan at 759 metres, is the 54th–highest peak in Ireland on the Arderin scale, and the 70th–highest peak on the Vandeleur-Lynam scale.

trails.name: Purple Mountain NE Top summit
trails.why: Purple Mountain at 832 metres high, is the 21st–highest peak in Ireland on the Arderin scale, and the 28th–highest according to the Vandeleur-Lynam scale.

trails.name: Errigal summit
trails.why: Errigal is a 751-metre mountain near Gweedore in County Donegal, Ireland. It is the tallest peak of the Derryveagh Mountains and the tallest peak in County Donegal.

trails.name: Blackstairs Mountain summit
trails.why: Blackstairs Mountain in southern Leinster, is the second-highest mountain in the Blackstairs Mountains.

trails.name: Benbaun summit
trails.why: Benbaun at 729 metres, is the 72nd–highest peak in Ireland on the Arderin scale, and the 88th–highest peak on the Vandeleur-Lynam scale.

trails.name: Duff Hill
trails.why: Duff Hill at 720 metres, is the 78th-highest peak in Ireland on the Arderin scale, and the 97th-highest peak on the Vandeleur-Lynam scale.

trails.name: Gravale summit
trails.why: Gravale at 718 metres, is the 79th–highest peak in Ireland on the Arderin scale, and the 98th–highest peak on the Vandeleur-Lynam scale.

trails.name: Bencorr summit
trails.why: Bencorr at 711 metres, is the 82nd–highest peak in Ireland on the Arderin scale, and the 102nd–highest peak on the Vandeleur-Lynam scale.

trails.name: Moanbane summit
trails.why: Moanbane at 703 metres, is the 85th–highest peak in Ireland on the Arderin scale, and the 106th–highest peak on the Vandeleur-Lynam scale.

trails.why: Binn idir an dá Log at 702 metres, is the 87th–highest peak in Ireland on the Arderin scale, and the 108th–highest peak on the Vandeleur-Lynam scale.

trails.name: Bencollaghduff summit
trails.why: Bencollaghduff at 696 metres, is the 93rd–highest peak in Ireland on the Arderin scale, and the 115th–highest peak on the Vandeleur-Lynam scale.

trails.name: Benbreen summit

trails.name: Knocknadobar summit

trails.name: Benleagh summit

trails.name: War Hill

trails.name: Hungry Hill
trails.why: Hungry Hill is a mountain on the Beara Peninsula, County Cork, in the Republic of Ireland.

trails.name: Derryclare summit
trails.why: Derryclare at 677 metres, is the 119th–highest peak in Ireland on the Arderin scale, and the 145th–highest peak on the Vandeleur-Lynam scale.

trails.name: Slievemore summit
trails.why: Slievemore is the second highest peak on Achill Island after Croaghaun, in County Mayo, Ireland.

trails.name: Letterbreckaun summit
trails.why: Letterbreckaun at 677 metres, is the 129th–highest peak in Ireland on the Arderin scale, and the 159th–highest peak on the Vandeleur-Lynam scale.

trails.name: Tonduff summit
trails.why: Tonduff at 642 metres, is the 169th–highest peak in Ireland on the Arderin scale, and the 202nd–highest peak on the Vandeleur-Lynam scale.

trails.name: Leenaun Hill
trails.why: Leenaun Hill at 618 metres, is the 201st–highest peak in Ireland on the Arderin scale, and the 243rd–highest peak on the Vandeleur-Lynam scale.

trails.name: Slieve Snaght summit
trails.why: Slieve Snaght is a mountain in the middle of the Inishowen peninsula of County Donegal, Ireland.

trails.name: Knocknahillion summit
trails.why: Knocknahillion at 607 metres, is the 210th–highest peak in Ireland on the Arderin scale, and the 256th–highest peak on the Vandeleur-Lynam scale.

trails.name: Aghla More summit
trails.why: Aghla More is a mountain in County Donegal, Ireland with a height of 581 metres.

trails.name: Ben Goram summit
trails.why: A footpath to the summit: 4.1 km each way, +391 m, up to 736 m, from near Castlebar along Cosán Phádraig.

trails.name: Glenmacnass Waterfall
trails.why: Glenmacnass Waterfall is an 80-metre high waterfall situated at the head of the Glenmacnass Valley in the Wicklow Mountains in Ireland.
